questions.q: Untreated sewage is discharged into a stream in Ibadan. Which change is most directly expected in the water immediately downstream?
options: The water becomes more alkaline because sewage is basic.
questions.explanation: Sewage contains much organic matter, so microorganisms multiply and decompose it, using up dissolved oxygen. This raises the biochemical oxygen demand and tends to lower the dissolved oxygen concentration.

questions.q: Waterlogged soil in a rice field in Kebbi undergoes anaerobic decay of plant material. The colourless gas released in large amounts that is also the main constituent of natural gas is
questions.explanation: Anaerobic bacteria in waterlogged soil produce methane, CH₄, which is the main constituent of natural gas. Carbon dioxide may also be produced, but it is not the main constituent of natural gas.

questions.q: An engineering firm in Lagos needs a strong, low-density alloy for aircraft parts. Which alloy is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Duralumin is an aluminium alloy containing copper and magnesium; it has a high strength-to-weight ratio and is used in aircraft construction. Brass and bronze are copper alloys, while cast iron is dense and heavy.

questions.q: The electron configuration of an atom is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁵. To which group and period does the atom belong?
questions.explanation: The atom has 17 electrons, with seven valence electrons in the 3s and 3p subshells. Its outermost occupied shell is the third shell, so it is in Group 17 and Period 3.

questions.q: A student in Abeokuta warms 200 g of water from 25.0 °C to 45.0 °C. Calculate the heat absorbed by the water. (Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed q = mcΔT = 200 g × 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹ × 20.0 °C = 16 800 J = 16.8 kJ.

questions.q: A student in Aba passes sulphur(IV) oxide into water and tests the resulting solution. Which observation shows that the solution can act as a reducing agent?
options: It decolourises acidified potassium permanganate solution.
It turns red litmus paper blue.
It gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution.
questions.explanation: Sulphur(IV) oxide reduces the purple permanganate ion to the almost colourless manganese(II) ion, so the solution is decolourised. Its action on lime water shows acidic oxide behaviour, not reducing ability. Red litmus turning blue would indicate an alkali, while the solution is acidic.

questions.q: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute sodium hydroxide to form sodium chloride, sodium chlorate(I) and water. What is the oxidation number change of chlorine in this reaction?
options: It changes from −1 to 0 and also from +1 to 0.
It changes from 0 to −1 and also from 0 to +1.
questions.explanation: In chlorine, the oxidation number of each chlorine atom is 0. In sodium chloride it becomes −1, while in sodium chlorate(I) it becomes +1, so chlorine is both reduced and oxidised. This simultaneous change is why the reaction is a disproportionation.

questions.q: A student in Yenagoa bubbles carbon(IV) oxide into lime water and continues for a long time. Which observation is correct?
options: The lime water first turns milky and later becomes clear.
The lime water turns milky and remains milky permanently.
The lime water remains clear throughout.
A brown precipitate forms and later dissolves.
questions.explanation: Carbon(IV) oxide first precipitates calcium carbonate, which makes the lime water milky. With excess carbon(IV) oxide, the precipitate dissolves to form soluble calcium hydrogencarbonate, so the milkiness disappears. The precipitate is white, not brown.

questions.q: Ethanol, C₂H₅OH, boils at about 78°C, while its isomer dimethyl ether, CH₃OCH₃, boils at about −24°C. Which statement best explains this difference?
options: Ethanol molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another, while dimethyl ether molecules do not form hydrogen bonds with one another.
Ethanol has weaker van der Waals forces because it is a smaller molecule.
Dimethyl ether has ionic bonds between its molecules.
Dimethyl ether molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another, while ethanol molecules do not.
questions.explanation: Ethanol has an O—H group, so its molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other, making it harder to separate them and raising the boiling point. Dimethyl ether has the same molecular formula but no O—H group, so it cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself. Hydrogen bonds are much stronger than ordinary van der Waals forces between such molecules.

questions.q: Which species has a lone pair of electrons on its central atom?
questions.explanation: In ammonia, the nitrogen atom shares three pairs of electrons with three hydrogen atoms and still has one lone pair. In methane and carbon(IV) oxide, the central carbon atom has no lone pair, while the boron atom in BF₃ has no lone pair in its bonding arrangement.

questions.q: At 25°C, 18.0 g of potassium chloride dissolves in 50.0 g of water to form a saturated solution. What is the solubility of potassium chloride at 25°C in g per 100 g of water?
questions.explanation: Solubility per 100 g of water is found by scaling the mass of solute to 100 g of water: (18.0 ÷ 50.0) × 100 = 36.0 g. The solution is already saturated, so the mass ratio gives the solubility directly.

questions.q: A laboratory assistant in Jos has a mixture of iodine crystals and common salt. Which method is most suitable for obtaining iodine from the mixture?
questions.explanation: Iodine sublimes on gentle heating, forming a vapour that can be cooled and collected as solid iodine, while common salt remains behind. Filtration and use of a separating funnel require a liquid mixture, and simple distillation is not the standard way to separate these two solids.

questions.q: In a laboratory in Zaria, 100 cm³ of nitrogen diffuses through a porous plug in 20 s. Under the same conditions, 100 cm³ of an unknown gas X diffuses in 30 s. If the molar mass of nitrogen is 28 g mol⁻¹, what is the molar mass of X?
questions.explanation: For equal volumes, the rates are inversely proportional to the times, so r(N₂)/r(X) = 30/20 = 1.5. By Graham’s law, 1.5 = √(M_X/28), hence M_X = 28 × 1.5² = 63 g mol⁻¹.

questions.q: A 2.0 dm³ steel cylinder at 27 °C contains 0.25 mol of an ideal gas. Taking R = 8.31 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, what is the pressure of the gas?
questions.explanation: Convert the volume to cubic metres: 2.0 dm³ = 0.0020 m³. Using P = nRT/V, P = (0.25 × 8.31 × 300) ÷ 0.0020 = 311 625 Pa ≈ 312 kPa.

questions.q: A fixed mass of gas at 27 °C exerts a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa in a 2.0 dm³ vessel. It is heated to 327 °C while the volume is halved. What is the new pressure?
questions.explanation: Use the combined gas law: P₂ = P₁ × T₂/T₁ × V₁/V₂. The temperature rises from 300 K to 600 K and the volume is halved, so P₂ = 1.0 × 10⁵ × 600/300 × 2 = 4.0 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: Propene is treated with cold, dilute, acidified potassium permanganate solution. The main organic product is
questions.explanation: Cold dilute acidified KMnO₄ brings about mild oxidation of the alkene double bond to a diol, adding two OH groups across the double bond. The product from propene is propane-1,2-diol.

questions.q: Which of the following ions has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶?
questions.explanation: A sodium atom has 11 electrons; Na⁺ has lost one electron and therefore has 10 electrons, giving the configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶. K⁺, Ca²⁺ and Cl⁻ each have 18 electrons and therefore an argon-type configuration.

questions.q: For the reaction A + B → C, doubling the concentration of A while keeping the concentration of B constant has no effect on the initial rate, but doubling the concentration of B doubles the initial rate. What is the rate equation?
questions.explanation: No dependence on [A] means the reaction is zero order with respect to A. Doubling [B] doubles the rate, so it is first order with respect to B; therefore the rate equation is rate = k[B].

questions.q: For PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), ΔH = +92.5 kJ mol⁻¹, which change would increase the amount of chlorine at equilibrium?
questions.explanation: The forward reaction produces two moles of gas from one mole of gas, so decreasing the pressure favours the side with more gas molecules. A catalyst does not change the equilibrium position, and decreasing temperature favours the exothermic reverse reaction.

questions.q: At a certain temperature, Kc for H₂(g) + CO₂(g) ⇌ H₂O(g) + CO(g) is 0.64. A 1.0 dm³ vessel contains 0.50 mol H₂, 0.50 mol CO₂, 0.20 mol H₂O and 0.20 mol CO. In which direction will the reaction proceed to reach equilibrium?
options: Reverse, forming more H₂ and CO₂
Forward only if a catalyst is added
Forward, forming more H₂O and CO
No net change, because equilibrium has already been established
questions.explanation: The reaction quotient is Qc = [H₂O][CO] ÷ ([H₂][CO₂]) = (0.20 × 0.20) ÷ (0.50 × 0.50) = 0.16. Since Qc is less than Kc (0.64), the forward reaction is favoured until Qc rises to Kc.

questions.q: Sodium metal from a workshop in Aba reacts completely with excess ethanol according to 2Na + 2C₂H₅OH → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂. If 4.60 g of sodium is used, what volume of hydrogen is produced at s.t.p.? [Na = 23; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: Moles of Na = 4.60/23 = 0.200 mol. The equation shows 2 mol Na produce 1 mol H₂, so H₂ produced = 0.200/2 = 0.100 mol. Volume = 0.100 × 22.4 = 2.24 dm³.

questions.q: A 0.500 g sample of impure zinc dust from Jos reacts with excess dilute hydrochloric acid and gives 112 cm³ of hydrogen at s.t.p. What is the percentage purity of the zinc? [Zn = 65; molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³]
questions.explanation: Moles of H₂ = 112/22400 = 0.00500 mol. From Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂, moles of Zn = 0.00500 mol, so mass of pure Zn = 0.00500 × 65 = 0.325 g. Percentage purity = (0.325/0.500) × 100 = 65.0%.

questions.q: A school laboratory in Ilorin has a glucose solution labelled 0.250 mol dm⁻³. What mass of glucose, C₆H₁₂O₆, is present in 200 cm³ of the solution? [C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of glucose = 180 g mol⁻¹. Amount in 200 cm³ = 0.250 × 200/1000 = 0.0500 mol. Mass = 0.0500 × 180 = 9.00 g.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of the compound (CH₃)₂CHCH₂COOH?
questions.explanation: The longest carbon chain containing the carboxyl group has four carbon atoms, so the parent acid is butanoic acid. Numbering starts at the carboxyl carbon, and the methyl substituent is on carbon 3, giving 3-methylbutanoic acid.

questions.q: Ethanal is reduced with hydrogen in the presence of a nickel catalyst. Which compound is formed?
questions.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation reduces the carbonyl group of ethanal, CH₃CHO, to an alcohol without breaking the carbon chain, giving ethanol, CH₃CH₂OH. Further reduction to ethane would require much more drastic conditions and is not the normal product here.

questions.q: Propanoic acid is warmed with methanol in the presence of concentrated tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid. Which ester is formed?
questions.explanation: The acid part of the ester supplies the propanoate name and the alcohol part supplies methyl, so the product is methyl propanoate. The reaction is esterification, with water eliminated.

questions.q: In a silver-plating bath in Onitsha, a current of 0.250 A is passed for 32 min 10 s. What mass of silver is deposited? [Ag = 108; Faraday constant = 96 500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.explanation: Time = 32 × 60 + 10 = 1930 s. Charge passed = It = 0.250 × 1930 = 482.5 C. Since Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, moles of silver deposited = 482.5/96 500 = 0.00500 mol; mass = 0.00500 × 108 = 0.540 g.

questions.q: A limestone statue in Benin City is gradually damaged by acid rain. Which gas is produced when the acid in the rain reacts with calcium carbonate in the limestone?
questions.explanation: Acid reacts with calcium carbonate to form a calcium salt, water and carbon dioxide, for example CaCO₃ + 2H⁺ → Ca²⁺ + H₂O + CO₂. The sulphur dioxide in acid rain is an input pollutant, not the gas released by this neutralisation reaction.

questions.q: A divalent metal M reacts completely with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. If 0.12 g of M liberates 120 cm³ of hydrogen at room temperature and pressure, calculate the relative atomic mass of M. (Molar volume of hydrogen at room temperature and pressure = 24 dm³ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Moles of H₂ = 120/24000 = 0.005 mol. For M + 2HCl → MCl₂ + H₂, moles of M = moles of H₂ = 0.005 mol, so relative atomic mass = 0.12/0.005 = 24.

questions.q: A neutral atom has atomic number 15. What is the ground-state electron configuration of the ion formed when this atom gains three electrons?
questions.explanation: The neutral atom has 15 electrons, with configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p³. Gaining three electrons gives 18 electrons, so the ion has the configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶.

questions.q: A student in Minna reacts 0.020 mol of magnesium completely with excess dilute hydrochloric acid. The reaction releases 0.46 kJ of heat. What is the enthalpy change per mole of magnesium?
questions.explanation: Heat released per mole = 0.46 kJ ÷ 0.020 mol = 23 kJ mol⁻¹. Because heat is released, the enthalpy change is negative: −23 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.q: Ngozi in Minna bubbles excess sulphur(IV) oxide into limewater. Which observation is made?
options: The limewater becomes milky at first and later clears.
questions.explanation: Sulphur(IV) oxide first reacts with calcium hydroxide to form insoluble calcium sulphite, which makes the limewater milky. With excess sulphur(IV) oxide, the calcium sulphite is converted to soluble calcium hydrogen sulphite, so the mixture later clears.

questions.q: Dry chlorine gas is passed over heated iron wool in a fume cupboard in Ilesa. Which compound is formed?
questions.explanation: Dry chlorine is an oxidising agent and oxidises heated iron to the +3 state, forming iron(III) chloride. Oxides are not formed because the reaction is carried out with dry chlorine and no water or oxygen supply is involved.

questions.q: A farmer in Makurdi is advised not to mix ammonium nitrate fertiliser with slaked lime before application. Which statement best explains the advice?
options: Slaked lime is alkaline and drives off ammonia, reducing the nitrogen content.
Slaked lime converts ammonium nitrate to a less soluble compound.
Slaked lime increases the acidity of the soil and spoils the fertiliser.
Slaked lime reacts with ammonium nitrate to produce chlorine gas.
questions.explanation: Ammonium salts react with alkalis to release ammonia gas. Slaked lime is alkaline, so mixing it with ammonium nitrate causes loss of nitrogen as ammonia, lowering the fertiliser value. Chlorine is not produced in this reaction.

questions.q: A student in Oyo prepares a saturated solution of salt X at 60 °C by dissolving 80 g of the salt in 200 g of water. On cooling to 20 °C, the solubility of X is 20 g per 100 g of water. What mass of X is deposited?
questions.explanation: At 20 °C, 100 g of water dissolves 20 g of X, so 200 g of water dissolves 20 × 2 = 40 g. Since 80 g was originally dissolved, the mass deposited is 80 − 40 = 40 g.

questions.q: A laboratory assistant in Warri is given a mixture of ethanol and water. Which method is most suitable for separating the two liquids?
questions.explanation: Ethanol and water are miscible liquids with different boiling points, so fractional distillation separates them by repeated vaporisation and condensation. Filtration does not separate dissolved liquids, while a separating funnel is used for immiscible liquids.

questions.q: At s.t.p., 1.12 dm³ of a gas has a mass of 2.20 g. What is the relative molecular mass of the gas? (Molar volume at s.t.p. = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: The amount of gas is 1.12 ÷ 22.4 = 0.0500 mol. Its relative molecular mass is mass ÷ amount = 2.20 ÷ 0.0500 = 44.

questions.q: But-1-ene is treated with steam in the presence of phosphoric acid catalyst. Which compound is the major organic product?
questions.explanation: The addition of steam across the double bond follows Markovnikov’s rule: hydrogen adds mainly to the terminal carbon with more hydrogen atoms, so the OH group becomes attached to the second carbon. Butan-1-ol would be the minor product, while butanal is an oxidation product and butane-1,2-diol is formed with cold dilute alkaline KMnO₄.

questions.q: What is the IUPAC name of the compound with the structure CH₃CH₂C(CH₃)=CHCH₃?
questions.explanation: The longest chain containing the double bond has five carbon atoms. Numbering from the end nearer the double bond gives the double bond at position 2 and the methyl branch at position 3, so the name is 3-methylpent-2-ene; the other names either misnumber the chain or choose a shorter parent chain.

questions.q: For a reaction, the rate law is rate = k[P][Q]². If the concentration of P is halved and that of Q is doubled while temperature remains constant, by what factor does the rate change?
options: It becomes four times as large.
questions.explanation: The new rate is k(P/2)(2Q)² = k(P/2)(4Q²) = 2k[P][Q]², so the rate is twice the original value. Ignoring the second-order dependence on Q or ignoring the change in P gives incorrect factors.
